title: Azure.Storage.Blobs
description: Store and manage unstructured data in Azure Blob Storage with the modern Azure SDK.

data.text: `Azure.Storage.Blobs` is the modern Azure SDK package for working with Blob Storage. It provides async-first, strongly typed clients for uploading, downloading, and managing blobs and containers.
Use `BlobServiceClient` to connect to your storage account, then use `BlobContainerClient` and `BlobClient` to work with containers and blobs.

data.title: Upload and Download a Blob

data.text: You can generate Shared Access Signature (SAS) tokens to grant time-limited access to blobs without exposing your account key.

data.title: Generate a Blob SAS URI

terms.definition: The top-level client for interacting with the Blob service.
A client for a specific container in the storage account.
A client for a specific blob within a container.
A secure way to grant limited access to Azure Storage resources.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Prefer `DefaultAzureCredential` from `Azure.Identity` over hardcoding connection strings in production.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `BlobServiceClient` as the entry point for all blob operations.
The SDK is async-first and fully thread-safe.
SAS tokens let you share blobs securely without exposing keys.
data.takeaway: Azure.Storage.Blobs provides a modern, async-first way to manage cloud files in .NET.

data.title: Exercise: Upload a File to Azure Blob Storage
data.description: Create a console app that uploads a local text file to Azure Blob Storage and lists all blobs in the container.
steps: Create a BlobServiceClient using a connection string.
Create a container if it does not exist.
Upload a local file as a blob.
List all blobs in the container and print their names.
data.expectedOutcome: You can upload and list blobs programmatically using the Azure SDK.
